CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection symptoms.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Randy Gutierrez is a 5-year-old male presenting with upper respiratory symptoms that began last night around supper time. Parents report onset of runny nose with nasal congestion. Nasal mucous is currently clear. Patient has a non-barky cough. Patient has been pulling on his ears and rubbing his nose. Rectal temperature was 100.3°F. Appetite has been variable—ate well last night, consumed about 7 ounces from bottle this morning, then ate minimally with refusal of cereal. Patient is irritable and fighting sleep despite having energy. Older sister is currently sick, and patient had recent play date with cousin who was later found to have a sinus infection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, non-barky cough, ear pulling, low-grade fever (100.3°F), decreased appetite, and irritability. Denies barky cough.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap (infantile seborrheic dermatitis).

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol given early this morning for fever. Saline nasal mist used. Baby Vicks applied to feet. Humidifier used overnight.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently ill with similar symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Exposure to sick older sister. Recent play date with cousin who had sinus infection.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Patient breathing well. Ears: Examined and within normal limits. General: Alert and interactive. Scalp: Cradle cap noted to be slightly worsened compared to previous assessment.

RESULTS
COVID-19: Negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection with nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, cough, and low-grade fever. Likely viral etiology; no bacterial infection suspected at this time. Continue supportive care with fluids and rest. Saline nasal mist to continue. For regular cough, may use Zarbee's cough syrup at dose for children under one year of age. Prescribe cough/decongestant medicine (half teaspoon dose) to have on hand—use only if barky cough develops, then give half teaspoon for five days. Counsel against honey for patient (under one year); agave is acceptable alternative. For cradle cap: use Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength, not extra strength) twice weekly; continue soft brush and baby oil application; avoid eyes during rinsing. Reassure that improvement expected within six weeks. Watch carefully for development of barky cough. Return for follow-up visit in one week. Return sooner if symptoms worsen. Patient to be seen back in one week.
